title: Renal cell carcinoma and other kidney tumors
text: Renal cell carcinoma, or RCC, is the most common kidney cancer in adults. Other tumors can arise in or near the kidney and may need different care. A broad tumor label does not identify histology. Do not use an adult RCC treatment summary as a protocol for a child or for every type of kidney mass.

title: Risk factors are not a diagnosis
text: Smoking, excess body weight, high blood pressure and certain inherited conditions are associated with kidney-cancer risk. Having a risk factor does not mean you will develop cancer, and people without recognized risk factors can still develop it. Smoking cessation and management of general health are worthwhile but do not replace assessment of a mass.

title: When hereditary cancer assessment may be relevant
text: A young age at diagnosis, several affected relatives, multiple tumors or tumors in both kidneys may prompt discussion of genetic counseling. title: Fever or infection symptoms during cancer treatment
text: If you develop fever or other infection symptoms during cancer treatment, contact your treatment team immediately and follow its emergency instructions. Infection can be serious, particularly with treatments that suppress immunity. Do not take fever-reducing medicine just to hide the fever before seeking advice. Severe illness, confusion or breathing difficulty warrants emergency care.
